PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.

source_views.view: Remedies adjust the details of a karmic pattern, not the pattern; four ways to please a planet: gem (only for functional benefics), good deeds, mantra/stotra, deity worship. For Sun: deed - go to a temple, donate to a temple or help run one; deity - Shiva, Rama; mantra count ~6,000.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Sun: Frawley: debilitated (Libra), in an enemy sign such as Saturn's, in the 6th/8th/12th, or under Saturn, Rahu or Ketu (Ketu's close conjunction especially). Shows as low self-worth, weak will, dependence; the father may fare poorly.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Planetary Influences on Human Affairs, ch. XI 'Astrology as an Aid to Medical Science' and ch. VIII
source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 7,000 for Sun; PVR gives about 6,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 9,000 for Mercury; PVR gives about 17,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

source_views.view: Remedies adjust the details of a karmic pattern, not the pattern; four ways to please a planet: gem (only for functional benefics), good deeds, mantra/stotra, deity worship. For Saturn: deed - do some physical labour or help people who live by manual labour; deity - Vishnu, Brahma; mantra count ~19,000.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Saturn: Frawley: debilitated (Aries), aspected by Sun, Mars, Rahu or Ketu, or in the 5th, 6th, 8th or 12th. Shows as agitation, poor endurance, trouble with institutions and money.

source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 23,000 for Saturn; PVR gives about 19,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

summary: Remedies for Rahu are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Rahu is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: in the 5th, 6th, 8th or 12th, with a weak, debilitated or combust dispositor, or aspected by Saturn, Sun or Mars. Shows as anxiety, impressionability, confusion, unwholesome habits.
lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.
